proof.text: For every simplicial functor F, the defining join formula for Tw is preserved by postcomposition. The functoriality clause of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration] therefore gives Tw(j) over j^op x j, and its two projection squares commute strictly. The induced map into the displayed fiber product is consequently a map over E^op x E. The left-fibration assertion and the slice-collapse comparisons are inherited from that same node.

source.place: Subsection 8.1.1 and Construction 8.1.1.1; functoriality and the two block-collapse comparisons

proof.text: Choose a simplicial quasi-inverse $k:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ and coherent natural equivalences $kj\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal E}$ and $jk\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For either $D=\mathcal E$ or $D=\mathcal C$, write $q=kj$ or $q=jk$, respectively. The quasicategory $A=\operatorname{Fun}(D,D)$ exists by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The chosen equivalence edge and its inverse triangles make $q$ and $\mathrm{id}_D$ isomorphic in $hA$. Apply [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval] to $A$: for $J=N(\mathcal J)$, where $\mathcal J$ has two objects and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, it gives a map $J\to A$ with endpoints $q,\mathrm{id}_D$. Transposing gives $H:D\times J\to D$ with these exact endpoint restrictions. Only the endpoints are prescribed; no claim that its restriction to the chosen edge of $J$ is the originally chosen transformation is required.

source.place: Section 3.5, core and invertible-interval extension; use the exact J-extension statement of lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval

proof.text: Define $\delta:J\to\operatorname{Tw}(J)$ explicitly. An $n$-simplex of $J$ is a sequence $(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ of objects of $\mathcal J$. On the ordered join $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n]$, send both vertices $\bar i$ and $i$ to $t_i$. There is a unique functor with this vertex assignment, since every ordered pair of objects of $\mathcal J$ has exactly one arrow. Its nerve is $\delta_n(t)$. Precomposing with $\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta$ assigns $t_{\theta(i)}$ to both vertices indexed by $i$, so these maps form a simplicial map. At $\varepsilon=0,1$, $\delta$ gives the identity-arrow vertex at $\varepsilon$. This construction uses the reverse-direction arrows in $\mathcal J$ on the first block.

source.place: Construction 8.1.1.1; elementary degreewise construction for the nerve of the two-object indiscrete groupoid

proof.text: First $\operatorname{Tw}(D)$ is a quasicategory: $D^{\mathrm{op}}\times D$ fills inner horns coordinatewise (opposite reverses the horn index), and then the left-fibration lifting property of $\lambda_D$ lifts each such filler. For each $H:D\times J\to D$ of Step 2, define $B:\operatorname{Tw}(D)\times J\to\operatorname{Tw}(D)$ in degree $n$ by $(a,t)\mapsto H\circ(a,\delta_n(t))$, where $a:N([n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n])\to D$. The simplicial identities follow from those of $\delta$ and postcomposition. At the endpoints it is exactly $\operatorname{Tw}(q)$ and $\mathrm{id}_{\operatorname{Tw}(D)}$. Thus $B$ transposes to a map $J\to\operatorname{Fun}(\operatorname{Tw}(D),\operatorname{Tw}(D))$. The edge $0\to1$ of $J$ has inverse $1\to0$ with its two inverse triangles; their images give an equivalence edge in this functor quasicategory. The functor quasicategory assertion is supplied by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply this construction for both choices of $D,q$ in Step 2. Since postcomposition gives $\operatorname{Tw}(kj)=\operatorname{Tw}(k)\operatorname{Tw}(j)$ and $\operatorname{Tw}(jk)=\operatorname{Tw}(j)\operatorname{Tw}(k)$ strictly, $\operatorname{Tw}(k)$ and these two coherent natural equivalences witness that $\operatorname{Tw}(j)$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Construction 8.1.1.1; J-parameter formula using Steps 2-3, replacing the invalid Delta^1-parameter argument

proof.text: For any quasicategory $D$ and vertex $y$, put $P_{D,y}=\operatorname{Tw}(D)\times_D\{y\}$, with its first-block projection to $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. It is a left fibration: lift a horn against $\lambda_D$ over the pair consisting of the prescribed simplex in $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the constant simplex at $y$. Hence $P_{D,y}^{\mathrm{op}}\to D$ is a right fibration, since ordered reversal sends $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$. Its total space is a quasicategory by first filling the projected inner horn in $D$ and then lifting. The slice node says $D_{/y}\to D$ is also a right fibration of quasicategories. The target-fixed clause of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration] gives an equivalence $v_{D,y}:(D_{/y})^{\mathrm{op}}\to P_{D,y}$ over $D^{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking opposites gives an equivalence $v_{D,y}^{\mathrm{op}}:D_{/y}\to P_{D,y}^{\mathrm{op}}$ over $D$: reverse the quasi-inverse and inverse triangles, which reverses the orientation of each natural equivalence and still provides inverse data. All objects remain small in the fixed containing universe.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.10 and opposite-category dual, with the exact right-pinched slice fiber convention

proof.text:
Write $T_D(x,y)$ for the strict fiber of $\lambda_D$ at $(x,y)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to the two right fibrations and the equivalence $v_{D,y}^{\mathrm{op}}$ from Step 5, over the identical base $D$. The slice fiber at $x$ is exactly $\operatorname{Map}_D(x,y)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], whereas the other fiber is $T_D(x,y)^{\mathrm{op}}$ degree by degree. Thus the actual collapse map induces a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes
$$a_{D,x,y}:\operatorname{Map}_D(x,y)\longrightarrow T_D(x,y)^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
By the functoriality clause of the twisted-arrow node, these maps commute strictly with every simplicial functor and the induced maps on the specified vertex fibers. The natural right-pinch homotopy equivalence of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] also gives the natural zigzag $T_D(x,y)^{\mathrm{op}}\leftarrow\operatorname{Map}_D(x,y)\to U_D(x,y)$ to the arrow mapping space. In degree zero both comparison maps send an edge to that same edge; in particular they preserve the identity-arrow vertices. This uses the target-fixed slice, so no identification of a left-pinched mapping complex with a right-pinched one is being assumed.

source.place: Corollary 4.5.3.31, right-fibration fiber invariance; right-pinch comparison 01L5

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the equivalence $j$ induces a weak equivalence $m:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(jx,jy)$; this is a theorem about functor equivalences, not part of their definition. Let $t:T_{\mathcal E}(x,y)\to T_{\mathcal C}(jx,jy)$ be the fiber map of Step 1. Strict naturality in Step 6 gives $t^{\mathrm{op}}a_{\mathcal E,x,y}=a_{\mathcal C,jx,jy}m$. Each $a$ is a weak equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak], applied to the inverse and homotopies from Step 6. Since $t^{\mathrm{op}}a_{\mathcal E,x,y}=a_{\mathcal C,jx,jy}m$ is a composite of weak equivalences and $a_{\mathcal E,x,y}$ is one, two-out-of-three for the weak homotopy equivalences of the Kan--Quillen model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] (the same realization-based notion, at every basepoint) proves that $t^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a weak equivalence. The homeomorphism $|K^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|K|$ reverses barycentric coordinates on each simplex; the realization relation for $\theta$ becomes that for $i\mapsto n-\theta(m-i)$, so it is well defined, involutive and natural in $K$. Consequently $t$ is a weak equivalence too. This same natural square, or its zigzag to the arrow mapping spaces from Step 6, identifies the map with the stated mapping-space map induced by $j$, including the identity vertices.

source.place: Natural right-pinch comparisons and functor-equivalence mapping-space theorem; elementary opposite-realization coordinate reversal

proof.text: Put $B=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E$ and $Q=B\times_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$. The projection $Q\to B$ is a left fibration by pulling each horn problem back to $\lambda_{\mathcal C}$; $\lambda_{\mathcal E}$ is a left fibration by the twisted-arrow node. The comparison $w:\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal E)\to Q$ of Step 1 is over the exact base $B$. At $(x,y)$ its fiber map is precisely $t$ from Step 7, since the fiber of $Q$ is $T_{\mathcal C}(jx,jy)$ by the degreewise pullback definition. The left-fibration criterion in the final paragraph of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] therefore gives a simplicial inverse to $w$ up to simplicial homotopies over $B$. This is the required equivalence of left fibrations. Its fiber identification is the one established in Steps 6-7; together with Step 4, this proves every clause.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.1.11; fiberwise criterion for equivalences of left fibrations

title: Twisted-arrow invariance under equivalence
statement: Use quasicategories, mapping spaces and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the twisted-arrow left fibrations $\lambda_{\mathcal D}:\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal D)\to\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal D$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Let $j:\mathcal E\to\mathcal C$ be an equivalence of small quasicategories in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Postcomposition with $j$ defines $\operatorname{Tw}(j)$, commuting with the two projections. This is an equivalence of quasicategories. Moreover its comparison map $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal E)\to(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E)\times_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal C}\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence of left fibrations over $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal E$. On each vertex fiber $(x,y)$ it agrees, under the natural slice and mapping-space comparisons, with the weak equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(jx,jy)$ induced by $j$.

source.place: Subsection 8.1.1 (03JF), Construction 8.1.1.1 (functorial twisted arrows), Proposition 8.1.1.11 (03JQ, left fibration), together with the slice comparisons; equivalence invariance is the auxiliary argument extracted from the item, not the statement of 03JQ.
